articles.title: Washington Spirit provide hope and joy in a city that badly needs it
articles.summary: Spirit’s run to the NWSL Championship final is in part based on a positive connection with fans at a time when DC is troubled in more ways than one. In the moments after the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals last weekend, all of Audi Field was in rapture.
body: order, the Spirit’s players made their way to the north end of the stadium, taking their celebrations into the crowd with their supporters. Perhaps no player has done more to push the Spirit into not only local but national relevance than US women’s national team forward Trinity Rodman, and Rodman herself grabbed a flag from a fan, jubilantly waving it above the crowd. Moments later, she bolted back onto the field and track down the club’s owner, Michele Kang, cajoling the businesswoman into a celebratory dance.

In the echo of all of this, many media members covering the match in the press box received an email from DC United, the local Major League Soccer club that operates and rents out Audi Field to the Spirit. It was a press release announcing the dismissal of their head coach, René Weiler. As the Spirit celebrated a third consecutive championship appearance on the pitch below, some unfortunate soul in a nearby office was tasked with sending that notice, the final nail in yet another dreadful season. While the women have thrived, the local men’s team has not made the playoffs in nearly a decade.

articles.title: Pochettino the connector: will human touch lift Manchester United?
articles.summary: Argentinian has excelled in man-management – but will need his powers to energise new squad and impress owners. Mauricio Pochettino celebrated his 50th birthday in style.
body: For Pochettino, it was emotional. As everybody knows, the new Manchester United head coach is the kind of guy to well up when the speeches start, so imagine how he felt when he looked up at the big screen and a video montage of well-wishers started to roll.

Pochettino’s PSG players were at the party. There was no need for anything from them. But there were loads from those he had coached at his previous clubs: Espanyol, Southampton and Tottenham. One by one, the faces flashed up; too many to mention. And, of course, there were the jokes about how old he was getting. But the tone was of pure affection; appreciation, too. Some of the players laid it on thick. They could not help it. They know what Pochettino has done for them.

This is what total buy-in looks like and this is how Pochettino gets you when he finds out which buttons to press. It might be a third-choice goalkeeper. Or a global superstar – for example, Kylian Mbappé, who Pochettino had at PSG. There is a story from those days that is worth sharing. Pochettino was due to give an interview and told the TV crew he would get Mbappé along to speak to them as well.

articles.title: Lampard calls for fairness after Coventry penalty row
articles.summary: Coventry boss Frank Lampard wants officials to spend time ensuring they get decisions correct in the wake of his side being denied a penalty at Everton.
body: Frustrated Frank Lampard has called for fairness from officials after Coventry were denied a clear penalty - with the boss claiming it got less coverage because they are a smaller club.
The Sky Blues were furious they were not awarded a first-half spot kick in the 3-1 defeat at Everton before the international break.
James Tarkowski pulled Caleb Yirenkyi's hair in the area but was not penalised by referee Stuart Attwell or video assistant referee (VAR) Timothy Wood.
The Key Match Incidents Panel, which assesses the contentious incidents and whether the officials got them correct, this week voted unanimously that the Sky Blues should have been awarded a penalty.

articles.title: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet
articles.summary: The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player. Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of…
body: He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session.
“We’ll do maybe two days on, one day off, and then three days on, one day off,” says Peters. “We’ve been doing that for just over a year now. It’s full-on. It’s pretty much as if you were at a club.”

Dele rose as a teenager to a level of stardom few experience and, used to media attention, doesn’t mind that his absence from football draws scrutiny. But he disagrees with the suggestion that choosing to stream on Twitch is a sign he has lost interest in the game that made him wealthy enough to never need to work again.

articles.title: The Super Bowl of F1: how Las Vegas GP has hit the jackpot after turbulent start
articles.summary: George Russell calls it the biggest race on the Formula One calendar bar Monaco – and the numbers back him up. That Formula One has achieved a palpable success in hosting a race in Las Vegas is impossible to ignore.
body: Long queues stretched out into the streets before the gates were even open and it seems many locals who were initially cool to the somewhat disruptive F1 circus have embraced the fans, their fervour for the sport and the positive impact of the race.

Kimi Antonelli tied up the title with Mercedes in Mexico but this weekend’s race in Las Vegas retains an unmistakable celebratory atmosphere that the organisers have assiduously cultivated and is, quite literally, paying off. When darkness falls and the city truly comes alive, adorned in all of its garish neon beauty, F1 in Vegas really begins to make sense as part of a burgeoning sport riding a wave of commercial success.
Las Vegas is now entering its fourth year on the calendar with a deal to continue until 2037. It is – for all that purists may dislike its emphasis on being, whisper it, entertaining – here to stay.

As Mercedes’ George Russell observed this week: “With where the sport is now, I think you need a race like this on the schedule. I guess it’s the biggest one, bar Monaco, from an entertainment perspective for the people who come here and for F1. This just feels like the Super Bowl.”

articles.title: Hazlewood backs Cummins to remain as Test captain after sandpaper 'pile-on'
articles.summary: Josh Hazlewood has defended Pat Cummins over a “pile-on” around Sandpapergate and refused to rule out boycotting the Test team if he is made to step down as captain.
body: Hazlewood became the latest player to break their silence over his involvement in the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, which has dominated headlines again since comments from Australian team-mate Usman Khawaja in his new autobiography 'Sabr' claimed the whole team were aware of using sandpaper.

Cameron Bancroft plunged Australian cricket into further turmoil with a 4,000-word statement, backing claims "the whole team" knew about the plot and contradicting strong denials Cummins offered in his press conference a few days earlier.

Cummins had branded Khawaja's testimony "complete and utter nonsense" and "100 per cent wrong", leading Bancroft to go public with his story, while Australia's Test captain has had his future speculated after how he has handled the incident.

"It feels like it's been a bit of a pile on the last few days [at Cummins] from different people," Hazlewood told CodeSports. "I want to back Pat [Cummins] and everything he said in his press conference last week, everything he's done for the last five or six years in particular as captain.

articles.title: Alcaraz puts aside injury concerns to take apart Cobolli
articles.summary: A ruthless Carlos Alcaraz puts aside his injury concerns to dismantle Flavio Cobolli and ensure a perfect record in the ATP Finals group stages.
body: Spain's Alcaraz hurt his left hamstring in his previous match against Daniil Medvedev and had a scan on the injury on Thursday.
He arrived for his match against Cobolli with strapping on his upper-left leg - as well as tape on his right knee and a sleeve on his right arm - but was brutally efficient in a 6-4 6-1 win.
The seven-time Grand Slam champion did not face a break point and bludgeoned 29 winners in a 65-minute victory.
"I tried not to move that much. I tried to be aggressive, to dominate the match as much as I can," the 23-year-old said.

articles.title: Shevchenko lying about drugs test claims - Mudryk
articles.summary: Mykhailo Mudryk accuses Ukraine legend Andriy Shevchenko of lying about the circumstances surrounding the winger's positive drugs test as his dispute with the country's football federation continues.
body: Tottenham Hotspur winger Mudryk, who is on a season-long loan from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 to July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium.

In an interview on Wednesday, Mudryk said he blames the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) for his failed drugs test and subsequent ban, believing it entered his system while on international duty.
In response, Shevchenko, the UAF president, accused Mudryk's representatives of repeatedly asking for a UAF employee to "falsely" take the blame for his failed test.

Former Chelsea and AC Milan striker Shevchenko also said Mudryk's comments amounted to a "baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally", and called on the player to retract his words.

articles.title: England's Penge grabs PGA Tour lead as battle to keep cards heats up
articles.summary: England’s Marco Penge bolstered his hopes of retaining full status on the PGA Tour for next season by grabbing a share of the halfway lead at the RSM Classic.
body: Penge started the week 120th in the FedExCup standings and requiring at least a top-four finish to break inside the top 100 and guarantee full playing status on the PGA Tour in 2027.

A birdie-birdie finish saw Penge post a second-round 65 on the Stadium Course, one of two used at Sea Island Golf Club, leaving him in a four-way tie on nine under alongside Michael Thorbjornsen and Denmark's Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen.
"I'm in a bit of a weird situation," Penge admitted. "I missed seven or eight tournaments this year from injury and have some sort of medical exemption still, which I don't really know much about.

"I'm trying to feel like it's the last event, but at the same time knowing that I have maybe three or four, five tournaments to start next year that goes towards this year's ranking. There's a lot of us guys trying to keep our job this week and we're all trying to give it our all."

articles.title: V8 engines return confirmed in bid to 'reconnect with DNA' of F1
articles.summary: Formula 1 will return to V8 engines from 2030 in a move FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has described as "an opportunity to reconnect with the DNA" of the sport.
body: Earlier this week, Ben Sulayem teased the possibility of V8 engines ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, live on Sky Sports F1, with the sound of a screaming F1 car with a caption: "You spoke, we listened. V8s coming soon."

On Friday, the FIA announced a technical framework had been unanimously agreed between the FIA, Formula One Management (FOM), the teams and Formula 1 power unit manufacturers to move to a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 power unit.
The agreement means the more popular V8s will make a comeback in 2030, 17 years after the sport abandoned them in favour of "road relevant" engines, a decision already backed by several drivers.

The current power unit, which is around 53 per cent electrically powered, has been criticised by some drivers this year as it has led to an unusual style of driving and racing at some tracks, with the drivers sometimes unable to push flat out in a traditional manner.

articles.title: White Sox Double Down On Rays Hitting Philosophy With Kyle Wilson
articles.summary: They are simply hiring the best people who know how to build hitters. After losing Joel McKeithan to the St. Louis Cardinals, the team needed a quick fix. Instead of looking elsewhere, they went straight to the Tampa Bay Rays.
body: McKeithan was a key part of the hitting staff, but his departure left a gap. The White Sox filled that hole this week with a man who has spent five years inside the Rays’ organization. Per Yahoo Sports, Wilson served as a hitting coordinator for Tampa Bay. He will work alongside Derek Shomon starting in the 2027 season. The move is a direct response to the loss of McKeithan. It keeps the hitting philosophy consistent while adding fresh eyes. Wilson brings experience from the Seattle Mariners and Tampa Bay Rays minor league systems. He knows how to teach swing adjustability and pitch recognition.

Wilson is not a rookie coach. For the past five seasons, the Rays employed him as their hitting coordinator. His job involved supporting hitting coaches across multiple affiliates. He worked to keep instruction consistent throughout the system. According to Yahoo Sports, his duties included evaluating player development. He also helped translate hitting plans into practice for young players. The Triple-A Durham Bulls hired him as hitting coach in 2021.

articles.title: Bayern player ratings vs Koln: Nathaniel Brown scores but the German giants frustrated by injury to Harry Kane
articles.summary: Bayern Munich were held to a frustrating 1-1 draw by Koln at the Allianz Arena, a result overshadowed by a significant injury to Harry Kane. Despite dominating possession, the hosts struggled to convert their numerical superiority into goals after Nathaniel Brown's equaliser.
body: Bayern Munich’s tactical blueprint was thrown into disarray early at the Allianz Arena as Kane was forced off with a leg injury just 20 minutes into the contest. This unexpected pivot forced the Rekordmeister to operate without their primary reference point against a compact Koln block. The visitors had stunned the home crowd in the 12th minute when Mikey Moore clinical finished a fast break, exploiting a rare lapse in Bayern's defensive transition.

The recovery was led by Brown, who restored parity in the 37th minute with a well-taken strike from outside the box. Despite controlling 71% of the ball and completing a staggering 747 accurate passes, Bayern lacked the final-third ingenuity to break down the Billy Goats' 3-5-1-1 structure. Koln actually finished the match with a higher Expected Goals (xG) value of 1.98 compared to Bayern's 0.94, suggesting that while the hosts held the ball, the visitors held the real threat.

Urbig was largely a spectator for long periods due to Bayern's possession dominance, but he stood tall when required. He produced three vital saves. He could do little about Moore's opener which was a high-quality transition goal.

articles.title: Raiders List TE Brock Bowers And K Matt Gay As Questionable Against The Broncos
articles.summary: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and kicker Matt Gay are questionable for Las Vegas' game at the Denver Broncos on Sunday. Bowers injured his right ankle in Sunday's 21-13 loss to Seattle and didn't play in the second half. He missed the first two games of the season after undergoing knee surgery.
body: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Bowers "got lots of work in" at Friday's practice, but was tight-lipped about a decision on the player's status for game day.

Bowers has 50 receptions for 676 yards and six touchdowns this season. He was an All-Pro as a rookie in 2024, when he had 112 catches for 1,194 yards and five TDs, and earned Pro Bowl honors in 2025 despite playing in just 12 games — eight starts — thanks to a bone bruise and PCL injury in his left knee.
Gay, who has an injured right hip, returned to practice Friday after sitting out Thursday. He is having his best season in years, making 21 of 23 field goals, including 3 of 4 from at least 50 yards.
If he can't go, rookie kicker Kansei Matsuzawa could be his replacement.
